attributes.comment:
On July 10th, the Board of Regents for the Universities of Wisconsin approved up to 5% tuition increase for the 2025-26 academic year. For students to enter and remain in college we need to advance federal student loans, Pell Grants, and other financial aid programs vital for a students’ education.

The Pell grant works for America and Pell funding supports working and returning students attend and complete critical programs—education, nursing, and the building trades— that strengthen Tribal communities and empowers tomorrow’s workforce.

I am seriously concerned that Pell funding is at risk. The FY 2025 Continuing Resolution included no Pell grant funding increases, and the program faces a $3 billion shortfall this year, projected to reach $9 billion next year. Without additional funding, grants may be reduced, increasing college costs for millions. Congress can address this shortfall—at no taxpayer cost—through budget reconciliation. I ask you to support additional Pell funding to ensure all students continue to access affordable education and contribute to their communities.
